summary: Forgot-password + reset-password + SlowAPI rate limits tested end-to-end. Backend: 9/9 pytest passed (forgot returns reset_token for existing email, delivered:false with NO reset_token for non-existent email, reset succeeds and enables login with new password, reused token → 400, invalid token → 400, short password → 422, login and forgot rate limits both trigger 429 with the expected 'Too many attempts. Please try again in a minute.' body). Frontend (390x844): all 7 UI flows passed — login-forgot navigates to ForgotPassword; forgot-email/forgot-submit/forgot-back testIDs present and working; submitting existing email navigates to ResetPassword with reset-token prefilled (len≈43); mismatched confirm shows "Passwords don't match." and reset-submit is disabled (opacity 0.45); matching passwords reset + auto-login lands on Home dashboard; forgot-back returns to Login. IMPORTANT observation on rate limit precision: with SlowAPI's default in-memory storage across multiple uvicorn workers, the FIRST 429 does not always appear on the exact 5th/6th login attempt (my run: first 429 at index 6 out of 15). The limit still triggers well within a minute for a single IP, but the effective throughput can be ~5*N/min where N = worker count. Not a functional break, but worth flagging. Credentials restored: alex+test1@jaleter.app is back to password123 (verified via /api/auth/login → 200) after both pytest cleanup and post-frontend restoration.

minor.issue: SlowAPI uses in-memory storage per worker; with multiple uvicorn workers the effective per-IP limit is ~5*N/min instead of 5/min. First 429 may not land exactly on the 5th/6th attempt. Consider adding storage_uri='memory://' explicitly OR shared Redis backend if strict-per-IP is required.

action_items: Optional: for stricter per-IP rate limits in multi-worker deployments, configure SlowAPI with a shared storage backend (redis://...) via Limiter(storage_uri=...). Current behavior still blocks brute-force in practice — no urgent fix required.

Before shipping to production: remove the reset_token field from the /api/auth/forgot-password response body (already documented as dev-mode) and wire SendGrid or an SMTP provider to deliver the token via email.
Consider carrying over the low-contrast Settings dark-mode issue from iteration_3 (still unaddressed, but cosmetic and out of this iteration's scope).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: forgot-password correctly protects against email enumeration — non-existent email returns {ok:true, delivered:false} with NO reset_token. Existing-account response includes the token only because we're in dev mode; documented in the 'note' field.
server.py: reset-password properly marks tokens single-use via {'used': False} filter + {'$set': {'used': True}}. Reuse returns 400 with 'Invalid or already-used reset link' as required.
server.py: password_resets collection has TTL index on expires_at (expireAfterSeconds=0) — expired tokens are auto-purged by Mongo.
server.py: reset-password ALSO invalidates all existing Google sessions for the user (delete_many on user_sessions.user_id) — nice hardening for account takeover recovery.

AuthContext.tsx: requestPasswordReset and resetPassword wrapped correctly with error propagation via callApi's thrown Error(detail). Token from response is passed to ResetPassword screen via onSent — matches dev-mode flow.
index.tsx ResetPassword screen: valid gate requires token.length>0 AND password.length>=8 AND password===confirm. Correctly disables GoldButton and shows mismatch message inline.
seed_data_creation: No new seed rows created; used existing alex+test1@jaleter.app. Password was flipped multiple times during tests and RESTORED to 'password123' at the end (verified via /api/auth/login → 200).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Forgot/reset endpoints stable. Reset tokens are 43 chars (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)). Rate limits: login 5/min, forgot 3/min, reset 5/min — but effective ceiling scales with worker count due to in-memory limiter storage. Seed creds: alex+test1@jaleter.app / password123 (restored). If your next test suite hammers login or forgot repeatedly, expect intermittent 429s during the first minute.
rca_of_issue: N/A — all requested flows pass. The only observation worth flagging is the multi-worker rate-limit imprecision (see backend_issues.minor).
